correctness.rationale: The stated nine-column-symbol three-column domination test is equivalent to the Italian rule on C_n x K_2 for n>=3. Independently reconstructed all 729 triples: exactly 666 allowed transitions, all satisfy the proposed nonnegative potential inequality; exactly 161 are zero-cost. Independent SCC calculation finds cyclic components of sizes 12,4,2, whose determinants multiply to P(z)=(1+z)(1+z^2-z^3+z^4)(1-z-z^2-z^5)(1-z^4)(1-z^2). Independent zero-cost trace counts for n=3..6 give 6,12,10,34. Telescoping proves the minimum n, trace/log determinant proves all n, and primitivity plus Perron--Frobenius yields the unique dominant root of x^5-x^4-x^3-1. This is an infinite proof from finite transition classification, not extrapolation.
